title: Enterprise Audit Readiness: Access Control, SSO, and Key Management Acceptance Checklist
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: This ticket captures the product requirements, scope changes introduced during scoping, and an acceptance-oriented sign-off checklist for enterprise audit readiness for Private deployments. Focus areas: SSO (SAML OIDC expectations), RBAC role model and enforcement, immutable audit logging and retention policy, and customer-managed key (CMEK) / HSM requirements. Goal: produce a measurable acceptance checklist that the engineering and security teams can validate before enabling Private GA for regulated customers.
scope_changes: 2026-01-22: Added SCIM user provisioning requirement after SOC interview with large customer (they requested automatic roster sync).
2026-01-25: Narrowed initial RBAC surface to 6 system roles + custom role templates (reduced from freeform permissions to speed delivery).
2026-01-27: Deferred audit export to external SIEM connectors (Splunk/Datadog) to a follow-up epic; initial delivery will support S3/GCS log export and console query.
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML: Service Provider metadata upload and SP-initiated login exercise completes end-to-end with two distinct IdPs (Okta, Azure AD) in staging.
SCIM: Provisioning API can create, update, and deprovision users and group memberships in staging with >=95% success rate in test harness.
OIDC: Support for OIDC authorization code flow and id token validation for token-based console sessions.

RBAC: Role matrix implemented (Admin, Org Admin, Project Owner, Developer, Auditor, ReadOnly). Each role's permissions verified by unit + integration tests and manual role walkthroughs documented in Confluence.

Audit logs: All auth events (login, token issuance, role changes), admin actions (deploy, rollout changes, key rotation), and data access events are emitted with timestamp, actor_id, tenant_id, and immutable event_id.
Audit retention: Logs stored with immutable write-once semantics for configurable retention windows (default 90 days) and a minimum retention policy of 365 days for regulated customers.
Audit access: Console query and S3/GCS export validated; exported logs are encrypted at rest and maintain event ordering for replay scenarios.
KMS/CMEK: Customer-managed key integration supports envelope encryption, rotation with zero-downtime rewrap, and optional HSM-backed key provider (Cloud HSM / BYO HSM via PKCS#11).

KMS failure modes: Clear fallback documented; when external KMS is unavailable, system fails closed for keys used to decrypt customer ciphertext; admin-visible alerting and runbook exist and are exercised in HA test.
Security review: Architecture and threat model reviewed and signed by Security Engineering and Compliance with open risks logged and mitigations in place.
E2E tests: Automated end-to-end tests exist in CI for SSO login, SCIM flows, RBAC enforcement, audit emission, and KMS rotate-and-decrypt scenarios.
Documentation: Customer-facing runbook and implementation guide published in Confluence with example IdP metadata snippets, SCIM schema, role mapping examples, and instructions for provisioning CMEK.
Pen test: Critical findings from external penetration test remediated or accepted by security with compensating controls documented.

notes_and_decisions: Decision 2026-01-24: Default audit retention set to 90 days for non-regulated customers; 365 days minimum for customers who opt into enterprise retention in contract.
Decision 2026-01-26: Implement SCIM v2.0 endpoint and document recommended group-to-role mapping; fine-grained authorization will be iterative.
Trade-off: Full SIEM connector parity (Splunk/Datadog native sinks) postponed to reduce initial scope and unblock GA for early enterprise customers.
Risk: Relying on external KMS increases blast radius for availability; mitigations include HA KMS configs, rewrap caching, and explicit fail-closed behavior for decryption of customer secrets.
